item.title: Sic Mundus #1: The Neural Network as Oracle — AI and Religion
item.description: First episode of the Sic Mundus podcast. How large language models work, why they resemble oracles, and how they are being integrated into religious life.

What Makes Contemporary Atheism Different
item.description: Appearance on 'Fiziki i Liriki' (Scientists and Humanists), Radio Mayak, 17 June 2026.

item.title: SPEECH Podcast (Litres): What Is Religion and How to Create One
item.description: Interview for the Litres podcast on the nature of religion, quasi-religions, transhumanism, AI in spiritual life, and what it actually takes to start a new religion.

item.title: Does Religion Exist? Three Approaches to Studying It
item.description: Realism, phenomenology, and constructivism — three frameworks scholars use when approaching the phenomenon of religion. A breakdown with examples and criticism of each.

item.title: Interview for the project 'Where do Religious Scholars Work? Our Alumni'
item.description: I recently gave an interview to my alma mater. We talked about science popularization, changing professions, and good books.

item.title: The Main Myth About Religion: Debunking Primordial Monotheism
item.description: What primordial monotheism is, where the idea came from, why it appeals to people, and why ethnographic data refutes it.

item.title: Godless: A Brief History of Atheism from Antiquity to the Present
item.description: A survey lecture on the history of atheism and freethought: from ancient impiety to the New Atheists of the twenty-first century.

item.title: On Religion, Atheism, and Science: Interview for the Trickster Channel
item.description: Interview for Alexander Bydantsev's channel. On religious studies as a science, the Brights movement, agnosticism, scientism, and the limits of the scientific method.

item.title: Agnosticism: Between Belief and Unbelief
item.description: What agnosticism actually is, how it differs from atheism and scepticism, and why Bertrand Russell called himself an agnostic among colleagues but an atheist for public audiences.

item.title: Erasmus of Rotterdam: The Man Who Defined His Age
item.description: The life and ideas of Erasmus of Rotterdam: from illegitimate son of a priest to the intellectual arbiter of Europe. A close reading of The Praise of Folly, the dispute with Luther on free will, and Soviet reception.
